faults.detail: It says a cold reading set against a hot figure looks better than it is, but never says why the figures are hot: the limits are for a fault on a cable already warm from its load, when its resistance is higher and the fault current smaller.
faults.fix: Add two short sentences: the limits apply in a fault, with the cable hot; a hot cable's higher resistance lets less fault current flow.

faults.detail: "That one rule gives every factor you use" is too wide: the rating factors Ca, Cg and Ct are not given by it.
faults.fix: Narrow it to the factors for R1+R2 and Zs.

faults.detail: The slider is the cause (the cable's temperature) and the bar the effect (its resistance), meeting the design's 0.436 Ω at 70 °C.
The check asks which way a limit moves on a warmer day, with the wrong-direction slip and the hot-figure slip as distractors: reasoning, not recall.
Every figure comes from a cited constant or the (t + 230) rule; the example readings and the 15 °C test day are labelled practice values.
Bars are named Design and Reading; the thermometer marks say what each temperature is.

faults.fault: talks about the idea instead of teaching it
faults.detail: The handover paragraph runs the client's documents and the interval into one 30-word sentence that lists rather than explains.
faults.fix: Split it into short sentences, one item each, and lead with the point.

plainWriting.detail: "The design takes the declared Ze, which is a maximum, and the largest resistance per metre" carries an aside mid-sentence.
plainWriting.fix: Two sentences: the design uses the declared Ze and the largest resistance per metre. Both are maximums.

plainWriting.detail: Eleven footnotes, several on points he would not look up on a job (Regulation 641.1's purpose, the designer giving test-temperature values, parallel paths twice).
plainWriting.fix: Keep footnotes on the (t + 230) rule, the 1.25 divisor, the 80% rule of thumb, parallel paths once, the certificate's schedules and the 5-year interval.

plainWriting.detail: "Limits for a measured Zs" is used without a name he can look up.
plainWriting.fix: Name it once as [[maximum measured Zs]], the limit for a reading taken cold.

plainWriting.detail: No sentence names where a fact comes from; no talk of the course; the practice values and example readings are said to be so, simply.

verdict: Three faults to fix (the missing causal step, one false absolute, the run-on handover paragraph) and the footnote load; rewrite as draft 2.
